chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Why he left the road: the kids and Cab's California trip
summary: McRae joined ASCAP in 1945 and left Cab to be home, since touring meant eighteen weeks of theaters.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x:
And my ASCAP name --
I didn't join ASCAP until 1945, so you
see, just before -- I had wrote a lot of this stuff
before I joined ASCAP.
I joined ASCAP in 1945 when I should've
got in before. But I was so busy on the road --
See, when you get tied up with bands,
you be travelling all the time -- it's a lot of things
you wanna do home.
That's one of the reasons why I left
Cab Calloway, because I wanted to get back. I just
figured that my kids were growing up and I had been
on the road.
You know, when you go on the road with
Cab, you do 17 or 18 weeks of theater -- the same
way with Hamp, you know.
Same way we did with Chick and with
got ...
Ella. Especially with Ella (unaudible), you know, I
took the band and we'd go on the coast, we'd be
gone for almost a year.
And then, Cab wanted me to go out to
California. I knew that was gonna be a long trip,

because he was gonna make a couple of pictures and he was gonna do all the way in Canada -- all the way up in the northern part of Canada and all in Seattle, Washington, you know.
By the time we got back,-- it was like eighteen or twenty weeks of theaters and one nighters, you know.
Now we had worked our way into Chicago about fifteen theaters from Montreal into the middle east.
You know, around Cleveland. You know, we had Cleveland, Detroit, Chicago. We were in at the Chicago for two weeks (inaudible) Chicago Theater.
We had played the Panther Room for a month. We went out of Chicago, came back to the Panther Room (inaudible) that big hotel in Chicago for four weeks.
